description.content: The headless API is designed for implementing your own store frontend with the data of your store. You are able to call the Headless API directly from a web browser (such as within an SPA), from a backend server, or in-game GUIs.

item.name: /:basketIdent/packages
item.description: Add a package to the basket by its `ident` or numeric ID.  - Using `ident` is recommended, since it works for every package type. It is required for external packages. - Numeric IDs still work for standard packages.  To add a package belonging to a dynamic category, set `dynamic` to `true`. Without this property the API will treat the request as a normal package ID.

request.description: Add a package to the basket by its `ident` or numeric ID.  - Using `ident` is recommended, since it works for every package type. It is required for external packages. - Numeric IDs still work for standard packages.  To add a package belonging to a dynamic category, set `dynamic` to `true`. Without this property the API will treat the request as a normal package ID.

item.name: /:basketIdent/packages/:packageId
item.description: Sets the quantity of the given item in the basket. The user must be logged in before the quantity can be changed.  - `{packageId}` accepts the package's `ident` or numeric ID. Using `ident` is recommended, since it works for every package type. - Numeric IDs still work for standard packages.

request.description: Sets the quantity of the given item in the basket. The user must be logged in before the quantity can be changed.  - `{packageId}` accepts the package's `ident` or numeric ID. Using `ident` is recommended, since it works for every package type. - Numeric IDs still work for standard packages.

item.name: /:basketIdent/packages/remove
item.description: Remove a package from the basket by its `ident` or numeric ID.  - Using `ident` is recommended, since it works for every package type. Send it back exactly as returned; don't build or parse it. - Numeric IDs still work for standard packages.

item.name: /baskets/:basketIdent/dynamic-packages
item.description: Populates a dynamic category with custom packages for the given basket. Dynamic categories are created in the creator panel with the type `dynamic`, and are typically populated in response to a `basket.authenticated` webhook.  Requires basic auth: the username is the webstore identifier and the password is the account's checkout API key.  Once created, the packages can be fetched using the category endpoints with both `includePackages=1` and `basketIdent` provided.

Requires basic auth: the username is the webstore identifier and the password is the account's checkout API key.  If there are no matching goals, `data` is an empty array.

item.description: Gets a package from a webstore by its `ident` or numeric ID.  - Using `ident` is recommended, since it works for every package type. Send it back exactly as returned; don't build or parse it. - `id` stays numeric for standard packages. For external packages `id` is synthetic, so always use `ident`.  Note: this endpoint does not support packages belonging to dynamic categories. Use the category endpoints with `includePackages=1` and `basketIdent` to fetch dynamic packages.

variable.description: The package's `ident` (recommended, e.g. `pkg_12_456`) or numeric ID.

Note: this endpoint does not support packages belonging to dynamic categories. Use the category endpoints with `includePackages=1` and `basketIdent` to fetch dynamic packages.

item.name: /recent-payments
item.description: Lists the store's most recent payments, newest first. This does not depend on the sidebar's Recent Payments module being configured.  Requires basic auth: the username is the webstore identifier and the password is the account's checkout API key.  - Free, manual, zero-price and incomplete payments are never included. - Responses are cached for 10 minutes. - If there are no payments, `data` is an empty array.

query.description: The number of payments to return, from 1 to 50.

request.description: Lists the store's most recent payments, newest first. This does not depend on the sidebar's Recent Payments module being configured.  Requires basic auth: the username is the webstore identifier and the password is the account's checkout API key.  - Free, manual, zero-price and incomplete payments are never included. - Responses are cached for 10 minutes. - If there are no payments, `data` is an empty array.

item.name: /sales
item.description: Lists the store's currently active sales, in the same order as the control panel. No authentication is required.  - Only sales whose start/end window includes the current time are returned. Expired sales, future sales and Lighthouse sales are left out. - Hidden packages and categories (disabled, removed, unpublished, or inside a disabled category) are left out of every array. - If there are no active sales, `data` is an empty array.

request.description: Lists the store's currently active sales, in the same order as the control panel. No authentication is required.  - Only sales whose start/end window includes the current time are returned. Expired sales, future sales and Lighthouse sales are left out. - Hidden packages and categories (disabled, removed, unpublished, or inside a disabled category) are left out of every array. - If there are no active sales, `data` is an empty array.

item.name: /top-customers
item.description: Gets the customer who spent the most in the given period. This does not depend on the sidebar's Top Customer module being configured.  Requires basic auth: the username is the webstore identifier and the password is the account's checkout API key.  - `total` is in the account's currency, net of tax, and matches the revenue statistics in the control panel. - Free, manual, zero-price and incomplete payments are never counted. - Responses are cached for 10 minutes. - If there is no top customer for the period, `data` is null.

query.description: The period to rank customers over. `none` covers all time.

request.description: Gets the customer who spent the most in the given period. This does not depend on the sidebar's Top Customer module being configured.  Requires basic auth: the username is the webstore identifier and the password is the account's checkout API key.  - `total` is in the account's currency, net of tax, and matches the revenue statistics in the control panel. - Free, manual, zero-price and incomplete payments are never counted. - Responses are cached for 10 minutes. - If there is no top customer for the period, `data` is null.
